# Liquidity Deep Dive Analysis

Report 107 | Published 2023-04-02 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2023-4-2/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/107.json)

Liquidity constraints and defensive financials.

Concrete successes include the April TGA sequence, 2023 gold record, uranium breakout, 24-month Bitcoin gain and Schwab profit pressure. The continuing recession lean and asserted inability to sustain positive real rates fail. Schwab equity caution did not predict its later recovery, and the optional short stop would have been reached. Insurance and bank value opinions are kept separate from horizon-defined forecasts.

**Coverage:** All article text blocks were read. Ledger covers material macro, investment, and causal propositions; incidental descriptive statistics, boilerplate, and unreasoned position lists are excluded. Image labels were read, not image pixels.

## Claims

### 107-C01

**Fed balance sheet stays above trough**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Mixed |
| Type | forecast |
| Horizon | Next couple of months |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | 2023-qt-ended-balance-sheet |
| Source blocks | 15, 18 |
| Thesis family | 2023-qt-ended-balance-sheet |

Assets remained above the precrisis March 8 low through early June, satisfying the narrow next-couple-months floor. They declined within that interval and substantially thereafter, so the broader sideways/new-trend implication did not persist.

**Direction:** Not independently resolved; see rationale.

**Timing:** Assessed against the stated horizon: Next couple of months

**Mechanism:** A matching outcome alone does not establish causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Fed balance sheet](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/WALCL) | Federal Reserve via FRED | 2026-11-07 | Verified in the audit

Precrisis March 8, 2023 $8.342283tn; April 5 $8.632384tn; May 31 $8.385854tn; June 7 $8.389325tn; April 2, 2025 $6.723452tn.

- [Monetary policy implementation](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/speech/jefferson20260116a.htm) | Federal Reserve | 2026-01-16 | Verified in the audit

Balance-sheet runoff begun in 2022 ended December 2025; reserve-management purchases followed. This was more than two years after March 2023 stress.

### 107-C33

**Broker custody differs from bank risk**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Mixed |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | brokerage-custody-versus-bank-risk |
| Source blocks | 150 |
| Thesis family | brokerage-custody-versus-bank-risk |

Separating bank equity risk from customer securities is correct. SIPC protects missing assets, not investment losses, and assets above $500,000 are not automatically unsecured corporate exposure merely because insurance is capped. Custody and segregation deserve more emphasis than aggregate insurance divided by client assets.

**Direction:** Not independently resolved; see rationale.

**Timing:** No numerical deadline was stated.

**Mechanism:** See rationale; this is not a forecast hit.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [SIPC protection scope](https://www.sipc.org/for-investors/introduction) | SIPC | Verified in the audit

SIPC restores missing customer cash and securities when a member broker fails, up to $500,000 including a $250,000 cash limit; not market-loss insurance.

## Framework lessons

- Distinguish funding durability from credit quality.

## Verification limitations

- Captured website text is not an authenticated publication-date version.
- Chart-only numerical claims have not been visually verified.
- Selected stock/ETF adjusted-close comparisons are disclosed where used; no reconstructed portfolio backtest has been performed.
- Unresolved verdicts are not forecast failures or successes; no aggregate hit rate is inferred.
